$comment: Documented, EXPIRING exceptions for scripts/audit-gate.mjs. Every advisory
still fails CI unless it is listed here by its GHSA id and unexpired.
An entry is a risk decision with a date on it, not a mute button: when
`expires` passes the gate goes red again so the decision gets remade.
Never add an entry to make a build green — add it only when there is no
upstream fix AND the exposure is understood and written down.

accepted.reason: Uncontrolled resource consumption in zod array validation (advisory published 2026-10 — it went red mid-release on the 2026-10-23 dependency wave). NO fix on the installed line: the advisory range is zod <4.6.6 with the fix in 4.6.6+, and jimp 1.6.1 (latest) declares zod ^3.23.8 in every @jimp/plugin-* package — zod 3.25.76 is the newest 3.x and has no patched release, so npm's only remediation is a jimp downgrade to 0.22.12 (2023). MITIGATED BY REACHABILITY: every @jimp plugin uses zod ONLY for developer-supplied OPTIONS schemas (verified in @jimp/plugin-crop dist/esm/index.js: CropOptionsSchema z.object({x,y,w,h numbers}, tolerance 0..1, booleans)) — zod never touches image bytes or anything an end user controls, and the DoS requires a huge unconstrained ARRAY inside the validated object, which only the calling app could construct. Our own direct zod pin is 4.6.7 (patched). Residual risk: a future jimp release validating image-derived data with zod would re-expose it; the gate goes red again at expiry so the decision gets remade. Re-check at expiry for a jimp release on zod 4 (or a patched zod 3.x backport), bump, and drop this entry.

accepted.package: glob 11/13 (via mjml -> js-beautify/mjml-cli, vite-plugin-pwa -> workbox-build, @vue/test-utils -> js-beautify)
accepted.reason: AbortSignal cancellation bypass: a walk keeps traversing after its signal aborts (advisory published 2026-10-30T23:09Z). Fixed only in glob 14.0.2+, a major released 2026-10-27. Re-checked 2026-11-15: the consumers that moved to glob 14 were bumped (e2b 2.64.0 declares ^14.0.3; @googleapis/androidpublisher 42.3.1 brings gaxios 8, which no longer declares rimraf), and our direct pin (@molecule/api-database-postgresql) is on 14.0.3. The remaining consumers have no release on glob 14: js-beautify 2.0.3 ^13.0.6 (also the dependency of @vue/test-utils 2.6.0), mjml-cli 5.4.1 ^13.0.6, workbox-build 7.4.1 ^11.0.1 (all latest on 2026-11-15). UNREACHABLE AS USED: the defect needs a caller that passes an AbortSignal (`signal`) to bound a walk. Re-verified in each installed dist on 2026-11-15: js-beautify calls globSync on its CLI file arguments, mjml-cli calls glob.sync on its CLI inputs, and workbox-build calls globSync with cwd/follow/ignore from the build config; none passes `signal`, and the patterns are developer-supplied. Residual risk: a consumer release that starts bounding a walk with a signal. Re-check at expiry for consumer releases on glob 14, bump, and drop this entry.

accepted.package: minimatch <11.0.1 (via casbin, mjml-cli, js-beautify -> editorconfig, glob 11/13; dev: typescript-eslint, ts-morph, workbox-build -> ejs -> jake -> filelist)
accepted.reason: DoS through globparts amplification of a crafted PATTERN (advisory published 2026-10-30T23:09Z). Fixed only in minimatch 11.0.1+, a major released 2026-10-27 that removes makeRe(), Minimatch#regexp, the AST class and matchOne()/slashSplit(). Re-checked 2026-11-15: eslint was bumped to 10.15.0, which with @eslint/config-array 0.23.6 is on minimatch 11.0.8, and e2b 2.64.0 is on minimatch 11 too. The remaining consumers have no release that accepts 11 (all latest on 2026-11-15): typescript-estree 8.72.2 ^10.2.2, @ts-morph/common 0.29.0 ^10.0.1, casbin 5.51.1 ^10.2.1, mjml-cli 5.4.1 ^10.2.6, filelist 2.0.2 ^10.2.1, and js-beautify 2.0.3 pins editorconfig ^3.0.2 (editorconfig 4.0.1 is on minimatch 11 but js-beautify does not accept it). An overrides pin to 11 would break ts-morph, which calls makeRe() and reads .regexp. MITIGATED BY REACHABILITY: the attacker must control the glob pattern. At runtime casbin calls minimatch only in its globMatch builtin; the default model in @molecule/api-permissions-casbin matches with g() and == equality (re-verified 2026-11-15, provider.ts DEFAULT_MODEL) and never uses globMatch. editorconfig patterns come from .editorconfig files on disk, mjml-cli patterns from its command line, and glob's from the developer-supplied patterns above. The dev tooling only matches our own config globs. Residual risk: an app that writes a custom casbin model using globMatch over user-authored policy patterns. Re-check at expiry for consumer releases on minimatch 11, bump, and drop this entry.
